writeup.headline: Molina rates Hold, just above Sell: a net-cash balance sheet offsets thin margins, shrinking revenue and full multiples.
writeup.thesis: Molina scores 46, a Hold only 2 points above the Sell line. The balance sheet is the clear strength, scoring 100 with net cash and cash at 2.27 times debt. Growth (28) is weak, with a TTM revenue decline of 0.9% and a latest-quarter revenue decline of 3.4% year on year, though growth sped up by 1.4 pp from the previous quarter. Quality (40) reflects very thin margins: an operating margin of 0.4% and an FCF margin of 0.5%, partly helped by the diluted share count down 1.9% year on year. Valuation (34) is mixed. P/S of 0.2x is low in absolute terms, but P/FCF of 43.4x and EV/EBIT of 32.2x are high in absolute terms, and the stock is expensive against its own history: EV/EBIT is more expensive than at every one of the last 61 month-ends, while P/S is cheaper than at 47 of the last 61 month-ends.
key_risks: Razor-thin margins (0.4% operating) leave little room for higher medical costs
2027 premium outlook cut to at least $45B from $46.5B because of the Georgia and Texas contract delays
Exiting traditional MAPD and shrinking Marketplace to seven states narrows the footprint
New Florida CMS Plan is expected to run at a loss in Q4
Shares 8.3 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days and price 18.4% below its 52-week high
what_would_change: A 2-point drop in the score would move it to Sell, for example from weaker trend or news readings
Reaching Buy needs 19 more points, most plausibly from growth turning back to revenue gains and margins recovering
Earnings and free cash flow recovering would bring down P/FCF and EV/EBIT and lift the valuation score
Resolution of the Georgia and Texas court proceedings, which are holding back about $1.3B of premium, could improve the news and growth outlook
